thread:
Maya: Heads up — after rolling kernel-affinity v2 yesterday I'm seeing tail latency regressions on prefill-heavy workloads (~95p +30ms). Profiles point to repeated kernel hop for prefill/decode boundary. logs attached.

Leo: Noted. Can you paste the perf snippet?

Maya: ```
summary: run=staging-34
model: vicuna-13b-8k
prefill mean=12ms, p95=56ms
decode mean=8ms, p95=26ms
overall p95 jump +32ms after v2
kernel switches per request: avg 2.8 -> 4.1
kv warmups/sec decrease 18%
```

Rahul: Hmm kernel-selection heuristics probably lost affinity; did we change token_budget threshold?

Maya: Yes, the new selector prefers smaller kernels for >512 seq and we dropped token_budget_target from 64->48 in the prefill batcher to reduce batch size variance.

Jen: Could be hurting prefill because it increases kernel handoffs during long context warmups. Suggest split prefill/decode batch pools and set token_budget_target higher for prefill to favor fewer larger batches.

Kevin: Agree. Try prefill_token_budget_target=96 and prefill_max_batch_tokens=4096; keep decode lower.

Maya: I ran a quick A/B. Pre-change (v2) vs v2+prefill_budget96:
- v2: p95=87ms
- v2+prefill_budget96: p95=58ms
KV hit-rate improved ~4%, kernel switches avg 2.1.

Leo: Nice. Any regression on decode-only short requests?

Maya: Decode-only (single prompt ~30 tokens): decode latency +2ms median, p95 unchanged. Memory use slightly up but within headroom.

Rahul: We should add a phase-aware scheduler tweak: when request is identified as "prefill-heavy" (initial prompt tokens > threshold OR ctx_len > 1024) route to prefill pool with pre-warmed KV priming. Also add a short KV priming window (200ms) where we allow eager prefetch.

Jen: Implementation detail: add prefill queue tag, new enqueue policy FIFO with token_budget target high, and a kernel-routing hint header "kernel_hint: large-kernel" so runtime picks fused attention kernels.

Maya: Prototype config:
```
runtime.batchers:
  prefill:
    token_budget_target: 96
    max_batch_tokens: 4096
    queue_policy: FIFO
    kernel_hint: large
    kv_priming_window_ms: 200
  decode:
    token_budget_target: 32
    max_batch_tokens: 1024
    queue_policy: LIFO
    kernel_hint: small
```

Kevin: Also add metric: kernel_handoff_count by phase and kv_primed_ratio. We can gate rollout on kv_primed_ratio >= 0.6 and p95_improvement >= 10ms.

ops-bot: deploy queued: canary runtime-v2.1 to gpu-pool-3 in 2m.

Leo: I'll own the benchmark and add a synthetic that simulates 1:4 prefill:decode distribution.

Maya: Thanks. If canary looks good, we should also backfill regression test in our perf CI to catch this kernel-handoff scenario.

Jen: +1. Also add docs note for model-team about kernel-selector tradeoffs.

Kevin: Sounds good. Will follow up with PR for optimistic priming and kernel_hint header.

Maya: tagging @Rahul @Jen for visibility :eyes:
